question.text: Two beams of light having intensities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>I</mi></math> interfere to produce a fringe pattern on a screen. The phase difference between the two beams are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> at points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> respectively. The difference between the resultant intensities at the two points is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>I</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be _____ .

solution.text:
Given here, phase difference at point A and B are ϕA=π2and ϕB=π3.

Resultant intensity at point A, 

IA=I+4I+2I4Icosπ2

⇒IA=5I+4I0=5I

Resultant intensity at point B,

IB=I+4I+2I4Icos60° =5I+4I×12=7I

Difference in intensities is IB-IA=7I-5I=2I.

Thus, value of x=2.
